nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Did earlier studies investigate the effects of host-plant nitrogen fertilization across altitudes?
nodes.answer: No, earlier studies have not investigated the effects of host-plant nitrogen fertilization across altitudes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable agricultural practices|Companion planting methods_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What were the two levels of nitrogen fertilization used in the host plant treatments?
nodes.answer: The two levels of nitrogen fertilization were low and high levels of nitrogen, with the high level mimicking those typically used in modern agriculture.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable agricultural practices|Companion planting methods_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How many host plants were grown per treatment in the experiment?
nodes.answer: A total of 200 host plants were grown per treatment.
